item.title: Sometimes it's painful for me to do the things I must get done
item.content:encoded:
When I was a student, I got good grades in the subject I liked but I was having a hard time keeping up with the ones I wasn't interested in.
I knew that I had to study every subject equally, but I just couldn't bring myself to do that. It felt like dragging a labrador retriever refusing to move.

I know that once I start I wouldn't feel this way, but the act of starting often feels a lot to me. It's almost suffocating.

This tendency of not being able to start things I'm not interested in had huge effects on my life (e.g. taking entrance exams and job hunting).

After I started working as a software developer I managed to do what I was assigned to with the help of the environment(I think I got often hyper fixated) but I ended up having a burnout.

I read ADHD and the Interest Based Nervous System by Dr. Megan Anna Neff, and now I think these struggles of mine might be a sign that I have interest based nervous system.
I think her post helped me understand this trait of mine better, but will I ever learn to deal with this?
Do I have to live with it for the rest of my life?

item.title: Backrooms: It's good, but I got motion sickness
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

This month, I finally watched the movie "Backrooms". Since I watched the YouTube series in June, I had been wanting to watch it.

I had never watched a horror movie in a movie theater before, and I'm kind of glad that this time became my first.

I was surprised to see that there were not only adults but also kids in the audience. I wouldn't have been able to watch it if I was a kid(I heard a kid crying behind my seat when Captain Clark started chasing Mary. Poor kid).

It was exciting to find some elements that had appeared in the series! I could enjoy the movie more because I had watched the series beforehand.

However, I couldn't enjoy the first part of the movie to be honest... I got pretty heavy motion sickness from the video footages. I felt conflicted because I wanted to get out and take breaks, but if I did I would have missed important scenes (as the story progressed I felt better and could focus on the screen).

Oh and I got a sticker when I passed the entrance!

item.title: Why do I write? Do I even like writing?
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

It's been months since I started writing here, but to be honest I don't know if I even like writing.

I know I like discovering new things and places. The excitement I get from exploring those things is stronger than any other activities.
I thought I liked singing, but I realized that I liked it only when I felt I could sing well, and not when I was practicing.

Sure it feels better after I write down my thoughts and feelings on paper, but the act of writing itself does not feel as great as exploring or singing (it doesn't feel bad either though).

And yet I write anyway, because I hear that writing helps you think, reflect on your day, organize your feelings, deal with stress and understand the world around you better.

Also, sometimes it's fun to read things you wrote in the past.

Related

  • Note to self: please think on paper, for goodness' sake

item.title: How I discover new music
item.content:encoded:
I love listening to music.
These days I usually listen to Folk, Indie Pop and J-Pop.

When I want to explore new songs, I often check the "Release Radar" playlist made by Spotify, but sometimes I get bored of recommended songs and I feel that I should explore unfamiliar genres as well.

So instead, sometimes I read album reviews[^1] or ask my friends for some recommendations.

I also check:

  • <a href="https://www.last.fm/">Last.fm</a> 's recommendations

and

  • <a href="https://austinkleon.substack.com/t/mixtapes">Austin Kleon's mixtapes</a>

when I want to explore songs from the past.

[^1]: Reading album review on websites like <a href="https://www.rollingstone.co.uk/">Rolling Stone UK</a> helps me discover new albums that I can't find by just listening to the music picked by algorithm.

item.title: I buy less books lately
item.content:encoded:
This May, I wrote that I buy way more books than I can read.

I still buy books, but I buy less these days.

Maybe it's because I go to bookstores more often than I used to and I keep seeing the same books on the shelves, or maybe I'm more into the actual act of reading.

It's also possible that after I became unemployed, my savings are decreasing and I feel that I need to keep myself from spending too much money.
(Or maybe I'm just tired...)

I don't think this is a bad thing, it's not like I'm out of books to read. YET.

Despite all, bookstores are still my favourite place.

item.title: My Favorite Belonging: KODAK Film Camera M38
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

When I go on a trip, I prefer taking photos with a film camera to taking them with my phone.

This is the one I use:

KODAK Film Camera M38

Why do I prefer a film camera in the first place?

Firstly, the camera of my phone is not as good as the latest ones, because when I bought my current phone two years ago I bought the cheapest one at the time.

Also, I love the specific atmosphere that only film cameras can give.
I can apply filters after taking photos on the phone to make them look aesthetic, but it doesn't feel the same...

The first film camera I got was FUJIFILM's single use camera UtsuRundesu (写ルンです), I bought it when I was on a trip, and I loved how the photos turned out.
I was fine with buying it every time I wanted to use a film camera, but I started to want one that I can use repeatedly.
I don't remember why I ended up getting KODAK M38 though.

It costs much more than taking photos on the phone, and I sometimes fail taking them, but it feels nice to look back on photos I took with this camera.

It's one of the best things I've got.

item.title: Note to self: please think on paper, for goodness' sake
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

When I have to spend time alone with my brain, without books or a phone, I have little control over the voice in my head.
This voice — it isn't clear enough — has power to make me feel depressed.

For example, I tend to feel down as I read job requirements. It seems like the voice in my head is telling me that I'm not qualified for any job.

This is different when I write down what I think or what the voice says, writing helps me be more objective of the voice, my thoughts and feelings.
It keeps me from ruminating, which is I'm good at doing when I'm alone with my brain.

That's probably why I usually feel less depressed when I think on paper.

So dear myself in the future, please please think on paper, especially when you notice you're having negative thoughts, and try to stay calm.

Related

  • Why do I write? Do I even like writing?

item.title: I stopped using AI for writing
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

Because my first language is not English and I haven't taken enough writing classes, I'm not confident of my English writing skill.
When I started writing here, I was using Grammarly and ChatGPT to correct my grammar mistakes and rewrite unnatural expressions.

Then I read this post by <a href="https://enocc.com/">Pablo Enoc</a>.

  • It's Insulting to Read Your AI Writing [^1]

It changed the way I think about using AI and translator, especially this part: <blockquote cite="https://enocc.com/blog/2025-10-24-insulting-ai-writing.html"> No, don’t use it to fix your grammar, or for translations, or for whatever else you think you are incapable of doing. Make the mistake. Feel embarrassed. Learn from it. Why? Because that’s what makes us human! </blockquote>

I don't think I'm completely against using AI for writing, for I often can't tell the difference between the posts that's 100% written by human and the ones that's written/edited using AI.

However, I realized I was using AI to make the posts perfect. I originally wanted this website to be a place for me to play and experiment. That means this place is supposed to allow myself to make mistakes, and using AI is, I think, against this philosophy.

First I felt uncomfortable for not using AI to check if I made mistakes, but I got used to it.
Now, except for the posts published before June 12 2026[^2], I don't use AI nor translator for writing.

One thing I learned after I stopped using AI is that it's easier to publish posts, because there are fewer things to do before publishing.

I'm not saying that I will leave my mistakes untouched, I will correct errors and rewrite as many times as possible.

item.title: KOKUYO Sokuryo Yacho - a perfect pocket notebook for me to carry around
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

When I go out, I always bring my pocket notebook with me.
I take it out in a cafe, in a waiting room, or in a train (only when few people are around though).
I started carrying it with me after I watched video essays on pocket notebooks, and now it's my must-have.

I tried to carry around A5 notebooks, soft cover pocket notebooks and so on, but in the end I end up with KOKUYO Sokuryo Yacho.

Here are the reasons I love this notebook:

  • It's small and thin enough to fit in my handbag (and my pocket), but it feels like it has plenty of pages
  • Hard cover. I can write comfortably anywhere!
  • Beautiful color variations
  • It's cheaper than it looks (the basic one is less than 300 yen)!
  • Made in Japan. It feels nice to use something that's made in your own country, right?

Matilda Mann has been my favorite artist since I first heard her music (first I heard “Bloom” and “The Day That I Met You”).

Her voice, the sound of the instruments, the lyrics… everything hits the sweet spot in my heart.

“Roxwell” is her debut album, and it's one of the best things I've got!

I love this album so much (it's not every day that you LOVE EVERY SONG in the album!) that I even ordered a poster of Roxwell on the official site (although when you live in Japan like me, you have to wait for weeks for delivery :( ).

item.title: Adding "categories" section to Posts and Notes page
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

A while ago I added “categories” section to Posts and Notes page.

Visitors can click a category and jump to the category's posts.

The structure of the page is like this:

And here’s the css:

div.container {
    display: flex;
}
aside {
    @media (width < calc(768px)) {
        display: none;
    }
}
nav {
    position: sticky;
    overflow-y: auto;
    top: 0;
}

This is one of the features I wanted to add when I first set up this website, but lately I’m starting to feel that it’s unnecessary.

The "categories" section won't be displayed if the screen width is smaller than 768 px, so it’s usually hidden when you access the page from your phone.

Personally I use my phone more than my computer when I read posts, and I think that applies to many smartphone users.
So what’s the point of adding categories section that can only be displayed on tablets or computers?

I’m starting to think that, instead of adding the categories section to the page, editing the page like below might be better.

Once you click one of the categories,

the list of posts under that category will appear.

I haven’t decided if I’m going to make this change yet, though.

item.title: The most exciting sci-fi I've ever read: Project Hail Mary
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

This book is so great.
I wish I could erase my memory and read it again! This is the kind of book that makes reading fun... Why didn't I read it sooner? From beginning to end, I wanted to know what would happen next so badly that I sometimes read the end of the page first.

I've read the Japanese version. It's divided into two parts, but I only bought the first part. I regretted that I hadn't bought the second part at the same time!

I don't think that I can write what I loved about this book without giving spoilers, so proceed only if you've read it (or seen the movie).

Have you read it?

Are you sure you want to keep reading?
Really?

<details> <summary>Continue reading</summary>

First of all, Rocky.
To me he was just a creepy creature at first, but as I continued reading, I grew to love him (I mean, who wouldn't?). He's kind and sincere, and he didn't give up even after his crew died (but he's not human so he might feel things a little differently than us. If he was a human he would have gone crazy or have committed suicide, right?).

Then there's Grace.
We learn that he really didn't want to go to space knowing that it would be a one-way journey. However, after becoming friends with Rocky, he decided to give up returning home to save Rocky and Rocky's home instead. This sacrifice is huge, and I could tell how happy he was when he found out that he might be able to survive!

The friendship between Grace and Rocky is so genuine and precious. They weren't scared of or vicious toward each other from the start; they built their friendship with respect and curiosity. Not only did they overcome the language barrier, but they even risked their lives to save each other (BFF for life)!

Now I have a question; why did only Grace survive and the other crew die? I thought that the other two crew members had the same gene as Grace, which would have allowed them to stay alive after a long coma?

I bet that if they all survived, the bond between Grace and Rocky wouldn't have been this strong. They might not have become BFFs if they hadn't been alone!

</details>

item.title: Keyboard shortcuts I use
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

When I was a student, I didn't know that learning shortcuts could be helpful, so I would use the mouse and click the "Back" or "Save" button every time I wrote an essay.
Now that I'm used to using shortcuts, using the mouse each time I want to save or edit the document feels like a waste of energy.

Below are the Windows keyboard shortcuts I've been using for years. I thought it could be satisfying to list them, so that I could see how much I've learned.

I can use this as a cheat sheet, of course!

General shortcuts

  • Ctrl + C to copy
  • Ctrl + X to cut
  • Ctrl + V to paste
  • Ctrl + S to save
  • Ctrl + Z to undo
  • Ctrl + Y to redo
  • Ctrl + A to select all
  • Ctrl + F to search
  • F2 to rename a file
  • Ctrl + B to make selected text bold
  • Ctrl + U to underline
  • Win + I to open settings
  • Win + Shift + S to take a screenshot

File Explorer shortcuts

  • Win + E to open File Explorer
  • Ctrl + Shift + N to create a new directory
  • Ctrl + Space to clear the current selection[^1]

Excel shortcuts

  • Ctrl + ; to insert the current date
  • Ctrl + : to insert the current time
  • Ctrl + Space to select a column
  • Shift + Space to select a row

Browser shortcuts

  • Alt + Right Arrow to go forward
  • Alt + Left Arrow to go back
  • Ctrl + H to open a browser's history
  • Ctrl + W to close the current tab
  • Ctrl + T to open a new tab

VSCode shortcuts

  • Ctrl + <code>`</code> to open the terminal
  • Ctrl + K, then Ctrl + F to format selected code
  • Ctrl + Backslash key to split the screen
  • Ctrl + Shift + P to open the command palette

[^1]: I've heard that this shortcut doesn't work in every environment.

item.title: I buy way more books than I can read
item.content:encoded:
I love bookstores; they're one of my favorite places in the world.

But there's this problem: I buy more books than I can handle.

I prefer buying books in person rather than online. That way I can flip through books I'm interested in and decide whether I should buy them at that time.

It's not common to find a book you've been wanting to read in a bookstore.
So whenever I find one, I cannot help but think "I might not be able to find the same book later!".
That's why I end up buying at least a few books every time I go to a bookstore.

Now I have a stack of books I have bought but haven't read yet.
I have to stop myself from buying more, seriously!

item.title: My current keybindings configuration in VSCode
item.content:encoded:
日本語で読む

I use VSCode for coding and editing Markdown files.

Here's my current keybindings.json:

[
    // `Alt` + `;` -> current date
    {
        "key": "alt+oem_plus",
        "command": "editor.action.insertSnippet",
        "when": "editorTextFocus",
        "args": {
            "snippet": "$CURRENT_YEAR-$CURRENT_MONTH-$CURRENT_DATE"
        }
    },
    //  `Alt` + `:` -> current time
    {
        "key": "alt+oem_1",
        "command": "editor.action.insertSnippet",
        "when": "editorTextFocus",
        "args": {
            "snippet": "$CURRENT_HOUR:$CURRENT_MINUTE"
        }
    }
]

The configuration above allows me to use these shortcuts in VSCode:

  • Alt + ; : current date in YYYY-MM-DD format
  • Alt + : : current time in HH:MM format
